label: LIVING_1: a timeless primitive predicate for operating from oneself
definition: PRIMITIVE. Lives g: g lives, i.e. operates from itself and not as moved by another (ST I q.18 a.3 co.: vivere dicuntur aliqua secundum quod operantur ex seipsis), with no time index. Example: an animal, a thinker; counterexample: a stone. The same content as DEF-LIVING, whose lean_declaration is the premise MotionMapsBatch1.ThinkerLives rather than a predicate; this record names the predicate used by the Dei Filius attributes.
note: Explicitly identified primitive (Encode first). Open semantic obligation: a typed account of operating from oneself that applies to an immutable being, without succession. Two open bridges constrain it: 'Whatever HAS_INTELLECT_1 is LIVING_1' and the sense bridge 'Whatever is in POTENCY_1 in no respect and is LIVING_2 is LIVING_1' (ad49ea00-287e-4c7c-8ab6-fe222d16d493), each giving a sufficient condition; nothing gives a necessary condition. Distinct from LIVING_2 (life present at some time of a duration frame), the conclusion shape of the existing typed route SelfOperationLife; see DISAMB living.
